products.name: Business Pro Plus
products.proposition:
The premium flavour of Business Pro: fibre (GPON) internet on Fortinet 90G/120G CPEs, with SD-WAN and FortiPortal, firewall, static IP, proactive monitoring, a managed FortiAP and optional Backup 5G.

Gives a small or medium business a secure, managed business connection it can run itself: one premium bundle instead of separate internet, security and Wi-Fi products, delivered through the Summary Order Fulfillment of the SMB Framework (Order to Delivery).

business_rules.statement: SD-WAN/FortiPortal, Firewall, Static IP and Proactive Monitoring are mandatory: checked by default and locked in the Automation Portal for Business Pro Plus bundles.
Speed profiles with an upload:download ratio of 1:2 are only for Business Pro Plus; the 1:10 profiles stay with Business Pro.
ECM suggests the Fortinet 90G below 1 Gbps and the 120G at 1 Gbps; FAP-23JF-E below 1 Gbps and FAP-431F-E from 1 Gbps.
Business Pro Plus CPEs are provisioned in the dedicated ADOM FortiManager cluster (platform type “Fortinet HE”).
SD-WAN configuration (overlay, routing, templates, security policies) is a Day-N service by the MSS team, not part of activation.
A lifecycle request is accepted only when the sub-orders it depends on are complete (pending-order validation matrix in CRMGW). An up/downgrade needs the master order closed.
An add-on can be added only when its service type's sub-order is closed: voice needs GSM; static IP and Speed Booster need GSM and GPON; SaaS needs GSM and SaaS; vSaaS needs GSM and vSaaS.
business_rules.source: SDD v2.3 · §P4 Pending Order Validation, add-on matrix

business_rules.statement: Amendment and cancellation are allowed until the point of no return agreed in the workflows. There is no amendment from the SMB App.
Dunning throttles Backup 5G to 5 Mbps with IN offer 854 at TOSS, and removes it at reconnect.
The new generic CPE rate plan for 90G/120G carries an exit charge of AED 650 (to be confirmed by the business), per contract period: no contract, 1 year, 2 years.
The 900/450 speed profile is not offered on the Fortinet 90G until it passes the lab test.
business_rules.source: SDD v2.3 · General Highlights, Speed Booster

business_rules.statement: Backup 5G changes IN only when the bundle has it. New activation and migration: UpdateOffer for the base offer (6980) and the bandwidth offer. Cessation: DeleteOffer for both. Up/downgrade: added as in activation, removed as in cessation, kept by swapping the bandwidth offer, absent nothing. External shift: runPAM resets the geo-lock. Dunning: offer 854 at TOSS, removed at reconnect.

For an up/downgrade ECM suggests the Fortinet 90G or 120G (FAP-23JF-E or FAP-431F-E) below 1 Gbps, so the CPE changes only when the target plan needs another model; at 1 Gbps only the 120G and FAP-431F-E.
A device added during faulty device replacement carries its charge add-on PO: Fortinet 90G AED 13,200 and Fortinet 120G AED 18,000, one-time.
The CPE exit charge applies to cessation and to up/downgrade when the removed CPE's rate plan is still within its 1- or 2-year commitment.
business_rules.source: SDD v2.3 · §ADO 438907, US 438909 · The applicable SRs are stated; the commitment test follows the existing exit-charge rules.

business_rules.statement: At the end of the contract, EHS moves the account to the non-commitment package of the same family (ccat_after_contract_migrate_plan) as an up/downgrade; from an old-model bundle, RTF copies the dynamic attributes to the new-model target.
A migration from a legacy product keeps the existing contract-reset and exit-charge rules on the removed devices.
Cessation is blocked while the activation is in progress: the customer cancels it first, each sub-order up to its point of no return, and the cessation then ceases what was fulfilled.
Port-out is fulfilled as a cessation without Churn & Exit retention; port-in raises the port request at master-order level, before the split.
The FortiPortal organisation is created with the customer's first site and removed only with the last one.

journeys.name: Faulty device replacement
journeys.description: A complaint for a faulty CPE or FortiAP: WFMS asks ECM for the eligible models, the technician replaces like for like, swaps the model when the current plan needs another, or adds a chargeable device; WFMS submits DEVICEREPLACEMENT to RTF.

Get the eligible CPE and FortiAP models

activities.name: Replace the faulty device
activities.description: Same model unless the current plan needs another (e.g. 1 Gbps down to 300 Mbps: 120G to 90G, FAP-431F-E to FAP-23JF-E). Device recovery stays manual.

activities.name: Add: new device with its charge PO

activities.name: Fulfil the replacement, as today

activities.source: SDD v2.3 · §P4 ADO 289225 · Closing is read from the other journeys.

a.statement: The reference says CWOM writes a milestone table and a database trigger feeds Felix. The SDD says CWOM publishes milestones per sub-order through TIBCO to BPM, after RTF's NotifyOrderCreationRequest. This catalogue follows the SDD.

conflicts.title: IBM BPM and Felix overlap

a.statement: Both are described as holding order milestones for tracking. The SDD reads them as BPM using a Felix stored procedure.

a.statement: eVEDA / vEDA, WFM / WFMS, B2B Web / B2B, CBCM / CRMGW. Treated as aliases of one system.

b.statement: eVEDA / vEDA, WFM / WFMS, B2B Web / B2B, CBCM / CRMGW. Treated as aliases of one system.

conflicts.difference: eVEDA / vEDA, WFM / WFMS, B2B Web / B2B, CBCM / CRMGW. Treated as aliases of one system.

conflicts.title: Who loads the basket for dunning

a.statement: For BAR_OG, NPTOSS, RECONNP and CESSNP, NPS (overview) or RTF (CWOM section) checks NEW_BUNDLE_MODEL, loads the basket from the CRMGW registry and adds the summary-order flags before CWOM.

b.statement: RTF won't load the basket for dunning: CWOM uses its existing registry until it is retired.

conflicts.difference: Whether dunning orders reach CWOM with a basket loaded from CRMGW, and by NPS or RTF. The journey follows the General Highlights and marks those steps inferred.

conflicts.title: What CRMGW returns as FPC_SITE for FortiPortal SSO

a.statement: FPC_SITE is sent empty in the SSO assertion.

b.statement: FPC_SITE carries every site name with an active Self Service Portal subscription, comma-separated, for the organisation's party IDs.
